goldens.comment: Using retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1 reads a possibly stale value and can lose increments under concurrency; consider an atomic increment via Prisma (increment: 1) to avoid race conditions (also applies to the similar update in the catch block).

The deletion logic in scheduleSMSReminders.ts incorrectly deletes non-SMS workflow reminders (e.g., Email, WhatsApp) that have retryCount > 1. This occurs because the retryCount condition within the OR clause for deletion lacks a method: WorkflowMethods.SMS filter, causing it to apply to all reminder types instead of only SMS reminders, which is the intended scope of this function.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P2 | packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:190 | A failed retry-count update escapes the catch block and aborts the remaining reminder batch instead of isolating this reminder failure. | adversarial | 0.86 |

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff, the catch block at line 186-195 adds a prisma.workflowReminder.update call to increment retryCount. This database operation is inside the catch block but is not wrapped in its own try-catch. If this update fails (e.g., database connection issue), it will throw an exception that escapes the catch block. Since this is inside a for loop processing multiple reminders (the loop iterates over unscheduledReminders), an unhandled exception would abort processing of remaining reminders in the batch. This is a real bug - the retry-count update should be wrapped in its own try-catch to isolate failures.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:39 | The retry-count deletion branch is not constrained to SMS and can delete any reminder type after two retries. | correctness | 0.93 |

adjudication.rationale: Looking at the diff at lines 31-44, the deleteMany query uses an OR condition where the second branch only checks `retryCount: { gt: 1 }` without any constraint on the method type. This means any WorkflowReminder (SMS, EMAIL, WHATSAPP, etc.) with retryCount > 1 will be deleted, not just SMS reminders. The first branch correctly constrains to WorkflowMethods.SMS, but the second branch lacks this constraint. This is a correctness bug that could cause unintended deletion of non-SMS reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: | P1 | packages/features/ee/workflows/api/scheduleSMSReminders.ts:184 | Retrying is not bounded when schedulers overlap because each worker writes a stale `retryCount + 1`, so concurrent failures can collapse increments and keep the reminder eligible beyond two attempts. | reliability | high |

adjudication.rationale: The finding identifies a real race condition. Looking at the diff, when SMS scheduling fails (lines 178-186 and 188-196), the code does `retryCount: reminder.retryCount + 1`. If multiple scheduler workers process the same reminder concurrently and both fail, they each read the same stale `retryCount` value and write `retryCount + 1`, resulting in only one increment instead of two. Combined with the deletion logic at line 37-40 that only deletes reminders with `retryCount > 1`, this means concurrent failures could keep a reminder eligible for more retries than intended. This is a valid concurrency bug with the non-atomic read-modify-write pattern.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new retry logic: incrementing retryCount on failed SMS scheduling (lines 178-188 and 192-200) and deleting reminders where retryCount > 1 (lines 38-42). This is non-trivial business logic that affects when reminders are retried vs. permanently deleted. The finding correctly identifies that there are no test files in this diff covering these new code paths. This is a legitimate concern about test coverage for new functionality, not a bug or hallucination.
